data.name: Baddar
data.gender_notes: Baddar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'bd', meaning 'to strike, to attack'. The name Baddar signifies a brave, valiant, and fearless warrior. In Islamic history, Baddar is the name of a renowned companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) who displayed great courage and bravery in battles. The name Baddar carries the meaning “Brave, valiant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Baddar usually hope their child will grow to embody brave, valiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of courage and bravery in the path of righteousness.
data.etymology: Baddar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Brave, valiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Baddar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Baddar, also known as Al-Madinah Al-Munawwarah, was the second capital city of the Islamic State under Muhammad's rule. It was established in 624 AD, following the migration of Muhammad and his followers to Medina from Mecca after the event of the Battle of Badr.
